newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates skid on reserve cut.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates skid on reserve cut.

text.p: * Reserve cut seen releasing 6.7 bln pesos

- Philippine interbank call loan rates skidded to an average of 10.8125 percent on Monday from 11.21875 following the one percentage-point cut in reserve requirements which took effect last Friday, traders said.
Done rates ranged from 11.0 to 10.78125 percent, with 30 lenders and 20 borrowers.
Volume rose to 12.771 billion from 7.665 billion pesos.

Apart from the reserve cut, liquidity had been rising due to the daily maturities of reverse repos which banks had not invested back with the Central Bank due to the 20 percent tax on these instruments imposed on January 2, dealers said.
Liquidity is also coming from last week's heavy dollar purchases of the Central Bank in its bid to contain the peso's strength.
"The question now is what would the Central Bank do to siphon liquidity," a dealer said.
Traders said they expect the Central Bank to soon hike its rates on the term reverse repos to attract banks to invest.
Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza said last week the 20 percent tax would make it more expensive for the Central Bank to siphon money for the longer term.
Meanwhile, the secondary market trading of T-bills had more banks buying T-bills before interest rates move lower with the reserve cut, dealers said.
A Reuter poll of six institutions showed bid rates of 11.20 to 11.50 percent for the three-month bills; 11.60 to 11.875 for the six months; and 11.90 to 12.40 for the one-year bills.
